lead: Santa Clarita plumbing deals with hard water, hot summers and homes from the 1960s to today. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Santa Clarita.
risk: hard water scale, slab leaks and water heater wear
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and water heaters
why: Newhall and older parts of Saugus and Canyon Country have homes from the 1960s and 1970s, some with galvanized or early copper lines. Valencia and newer areas were built mostly after 1980.
Homes sit on slabs, so leaks under the floor happen. The 1994 Northridge earthquake hit the valley hard, and water heaters must be strapped.
utility: Santa Clarita Valley Water Agency (SCV Water)
water: SCV Water blends local groundwater with State Water Project water from Northern California. It is hard.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Keep a wrench by your gas shutoff.
areas: PipeMend works in Valencia, Newhall, Saugus, Canyon Country, Fair Oaks Ranch, Sand Canyon and every other Santa Clarita neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Santa Clarita Building and Safety Division, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.a: Yes. Local groundwater and State Water Project water both carry minerals. Scale builds up in water heaters and on fixtures, so many homes use softeners.
